headline: Persistence is continuing despite difficulty—the difference between those who succeed and those who quit just before breakthrough
universal_truth: Most people quit too early; the prize often goes to whoever stays longest
fun_facts: Thomas Edison made 1,000 unsuccessful attempts before inventing the light bulb
J.K. Rowling was rejected by 12 publishers before Harry Potter was accepted
Research shows grit—perseverance toward long-term goals—predicts success better than IQ
discussion_questions: What's something you're glad you persisted with?
How do you know when to persist versus when to quit?
What helps you keep going when you want to stop?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Edison failed 1,000 times. Rowling was rejected 12 times. Colonel Sanders was rejected 1,009 times before KFC took off. The difference between failure and success often isn't talent—it's whoever stayed in the game longest.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Persistence sounds simple—just keep going. But in the moment, when you're tired and it's not working, quitting feels reasonable. How do you persist when everything says stop?
cliff.prompt: How do you persist when it's hard?

options.text: By connecting to deeper purpose, breaking goals into smaller wins, and building systems that carry you through low motivation
options.response: Yes. Persistence isn't white-knuckling—it's strategy. Know your why, celebrate small wins, and create structures that keep you moving even when motivation fades.

options.text: By having more willpower than others
options.response: Willpower helps, but it's finite. Smart persisters use strategy to conserve it...

q1.title: The Dip
q1.script: Every worthwhile goal has a 'dip'—a difficult period after initial enthusiasm fades. Most people quit in the dip. But the dip is a filter—it weeds out competition. Those who push through emerge with less competition on the other side.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "The Dip"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Small Wins
q2.script: Persistence is easier with momentum. Break big goals into small wins. Each small victory proves progress is possible and releases motivation-boosting dopamine. You can't see the distant peak, but you can reach the next ridge.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Identity Over Goals
q3.script: The most persistent people attach their identity to the effort, not the outcome. 'I'm a writer' keeps you writing through rejection. 'I want to publish a book' doesn't survive failure. Be the kind of person who persists.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Most people quit too early. Persistence teaches that the prize often goes to whoever stays longest. When you want to quit, remember: you might be closer than you think.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 188. Tomorrow, we'll explore changing when things change—adaptability. Until then, identify something you've been close to quitting and find one reason to keep going.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Dip Check - Are You Close?
growTrack.learning_objective: Evaluate whether to persist or pivot
growTrack.activity: Think of something you've wanted to quit. Ask: Am I in the dip (temporary difficulty) or at a dead end (fundamentally wrong path)? If it's the dip, identify one small win you can achieve this week to build momentum.
